transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Nina Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lydia Gomez (Orion - Head ML), Tom Breuer (Orion - Infra), Aisha Khan (Orion - Product), Victor (Orion PM)

Summary (auto): Quick walkthrough of Redwood Optimize for batching and prefix/KV cache. Discussed cost/latency tradeoffs, pilot next steps, security docs.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maria): okay we can get started, uh so today's goal is a focused walkthrough on the Optimize recommendations we discussed — batching and the prefix / KV cache approach and how that maps to cost models for a payments workload.
00:12 Speaker 2 (Lydia): great thanks, we've got the core infra folks here, Tom and Aisha are on to validate network/security parts, i'm mostly interested in latency tail and cost per transaction.
00:25 Speaker 3 (Raj): hi all, i'm Raj, i'll drive the technical parts. quick note, i'll refer to a couple internal slides and a cost workbook, i'll share link after the call. if transcription messes up, sorry, sometimes it says K-V cash or K-V cache spelled weird, it's KV cache.
00:40 Speaker 4 (Tom): thanks, also be aware we have a strict p99 latency target of 250ms for our risk-check API and we can't shift it by more than 30ms.
00:52 Speaker 1 (Maria): noted. ok raj, you want to start with the high-level batching model?
01:00 Speaker 3 (Raj): yeah, sure. so two orthogonal levers we typically tune: batching and prefix/KV caching. batching increases GPU throughput by combining tokens across concurrent requests into a single kernel invocation; it improves cost per token but can increase latency if we wait to fill a batch. prefix cache stores repeated KV cache entries for prefix-heavy flows, which for predictable prompts (like payment verification templates) can give huge token savings.
01:32 Speaker 5 (Aisha): can you give an example for us? we do a lot of near-identical prompts for transaction verification with small variable slots.
01:40 Speaker 3 (Raj): perfect example. imagine 8,000 daily calls, 95% share the same 64-token prefix (policy text + account metadata) then only 20-50 tokens of variable content. with prefix caching we avoid recomputing the prefix KV for subsequent calls so cost moves down roughly proportional to prefix length — in practice we saw 5-8x token compute reduction on similar customers.
02:05 Speaker 2 (Lydia): 5-8x is significant. what's the hit on cold-starts if a user hasn't seen the prefix?
02:12 Speaker 3 (Raj): good q. cold-starts pay the full prefix once; cache warms quickly if TTLs are tuned. Redwood supports both per-customer cache warm policies and shared cache warming during predictable windows. there's also a fallback route if cache misses spike — we route to a warmer pool or spike to hosted micro-instances to preserve p99.
02:36 Speaker 4 (Tom): what about multi-tenant isolation? we can't have customer A's KV stored in a shared cache that could be read by B.
02:44 Speaker 3 (Raj): understood — caches are namespaced by customer and optionally by model version; on Redwood Dedicated you can run isolated caches per-reservation, and for private deployments the cache lives in your VPC. for hosted we provide tenant isolation guarantees and encryption at rest.
03:01 Speaker 1 (Maria): i'll jump in with the cost model overview. raj, show the simple formula you use.
03:06 Speaker 3 (Raj): sure — rough sketch: total cost = base model tokens * cost_per_token + incremental tokens (post-prefix) * cost_per_token then divided by throughput gains from batching. but there are other factors: batch size, batch wait ms (latency SLO), kernel efficiency for sequence length, and KV cache hit rate. we put this in the spreadsheet so you can plug your traffic numbers.
03:30 Speaker 5 (Victor): can you send that spreadsheet?
03:33 Speaker 1 (Maria): yes i'll share it right after.
03:35 Speaker 3 (Raj): i'll also run an initial sizing if you send sample logs. even a 24-hour sample lets us approximate p50/p99 and sequence length distribution which is most important.
03:48 Speaker 2 (Lydia): ok we'll provide logs, need to scrub PII first.
03:52 Speaker 3 (Raj): totally expected, anything anonymized with request/response token counts + latency is fine.
04:00 Speaker 4 (Tom): networking question — if we enable prefix cache, does that increase inbound bandwidth / storage?
04:08 Speaker 3 (Raj): small storage footprint per cache entry (kv matrices per prefix), typically megabytes for large prefixes, but you can TTL aggressively. bandwidth is negligible compared to model traffic; most savings reduce compute more than increasing network.
04:20 Speaker 5 (Aisha): how does batching interact with our bursty traffic? we have spikes at end-of-day settlements.
04:27 Speaker 3 (Raj): important. Redwood's autoscaler + burst pools let you keep conservative batch wait times (e.g., 5ms) during normal traffic and open higher throughput pools during bursts. our routing can also degrade gracefully — if latency SLO is threatened, we lower batch sizes or route to lower-cost/high-latency variants.
04:48 Speaker 2 (Lydia): does that mean dynamic model fallback?
04:50 Speaker 3 (Raj): yes, fallback policies can be configured — e.g., 1) try primary model with caching, 2) if capacity constrained route to quantized variant, 3) if still constrained use a simpler model for non-critical fields. all transparent in the console.
05:05 Speaker 1 (Maria): i'll show a quick demo of the Optimize console (screen share notes). transcript may call it 'optmize' or 'optimize console' oddly.
05:12 Speaker 3 (Raj): (screen demo described) on the left we have workload profile, middle is batch suggestion engine, right is cost delta. key knobs: target p99 latency, max batch wait, cache TTL, and KV-shard size. you can simulate cost given a traffic profile.
06:00 Speaker 5 (Tom): simulation — can we upload our real traffic and run an offline sim?
06:05 Speaker 3 (Raj): yes, we accept CSV with timestamp, token counts, and route tags. the simulation will show expected p50/p99 and cost per 1000 requests.
06:15 Speaker 2 (Lydia): what's a typical cost improvement for payments use-case?
06:18 Speaker 3 (Raj): for prefix-heavy payments flows we've seen 3-6x reduction in GPU token compute and normally 40-70% $/req improvements when combined with sensible batching. again depends on model size and prefix ratio.
06:30 Speaker 5 (Aisha): any impact to hallucination or model accuracy when using cache?
06:36 Speaker 3 (Raj): cache only stores KV internal state for the prefix, it doesn't alter model weights or outputs. the main risk is stale prefix if you change prompt templates; Redwood tracks model-versioned cache keys and invalidates on rollout. we also support prompt diffs detection to warn about mismatch.
06:59 Speaker 4 (Tom): security question — we need KMS + HSM integration for encryption keys and audit logs.
07:06 Speaker 3 (Raj): yes, we integrate with major KMS providers and support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private. audit logs are exportable and we can stream to your SIEM.
07:14 Speaker 2 (Lydia): do you have SOC2/ISO certs?
07:18 Speaker 1 (Maria): yes SOC2 Type II, we've got a security pack i'll share.
07:22 Speaker 5 (Victor): any caveats on regulatory data residency for EU?
07:26 Speaker 3 (Raj): Redwood can pin deployment region; Dedicated/reserved capacity can be region-specific and Private lets you control residency on-prem.
07:35 Speaker 1 (Maria): ok quick live example: here's a real customer case (Finance customer) — before Optimize: 200ms p50, 450ms p99, cost $0.12/req; after prefix+batching tuned: p50 180ms, p99 260ms, cost $0.03/req. this is anonymized but similar pattern to what we expect.
08:02 Speaker 2 (Lydia): nice — can we see distribution of sequence lengths?
08:06 Speaker 3 (Raj): yep, in the workload profile here you can see a strong spike at 64 tokens for prefix and a smaller tail up to 300 for rare full-text cases. optimizing kernels for short sequences gives good perf.
08:24 Speaker 4 (Tom): about pilot sizing — what capacity should we reserve?
08:28 Speaker 3 (Raj): for pilot we recommend a small dedicated pool sized at peak QPS with conservative batch settings; we provide sandbox reserved nodes for a 2-week pilot typically. cost estimates will be in the spreadsheet.
08:44 Speaker 1 (Maria): action recap: raj will run the initial sizing once Tom sends anonymized logs; Maria to send SOC2 + pricing; Lydia to confirm success criteria.
08:55 Speaker 5 (Aisha): timeline looks tight but doable.
09:00 Speaker 3 (Raj): quick FAQ: quantization interplay — if you quantize model for cost, kv cache still works but kernel efficiency differs; sometimes quantized variant increases latency slightly at p99. we model that in the sheet.
09:18 Speaker 2 (Lydia): and what about embedding-heavy workflows? not our primary use but curious.
09:22 Speaker 3 (Raj): embeddings follow different pattern; batching helps massively but there's no prefix cache; Optimize has a separate embedding tab.
09:30 Speaker 5 (Victor): competitors — do customers choose openai for simplicity? how do you position?
09:34 Speaker 1 (Maria): most choose Redwood when they have predictable workloads and care about unit economics and SLOs; we beat generic hosted when customers need predictable p99 and cost control.
09:44 Speaker 3 (Raj): also many are hybrid — initial dev on generic APIs then move to Redwood Dedicated when they scale.
09:50 Speaker 2 (Lydia): any other Gotchas?
09:52 Speaker 3 (Raj): watch for prompt churn — if product team edits templates frequently, cache benefits reduce. mitigate via auto invalidation and template versioning.
10:05 Speaker 1 (Maria): ok we'll wrap with next steps and timeline.
10:10 Speaker 1 (Maria): to confirm next steps — Maria send security pack and pricing today; Raj run cost model after logs; Tom provide anonymized logs by Tue; schedule pilot benchmark for next week.
10:26 Speaker 2 (Lydia): we'll aim to have logs and success criteria by Tue, and Maria please add a couple slots for bench next Wed/Thu.
10:35 Speaker 1 (Maria): will do. thanks everyone, appreciate your time.
10:38 Speaker 3 (Raj): thanks all, i'll share the spreadsheet link in the notes.
10:42 Speaker 2 (Lydia): thanks.
